name_full: d-APV (stored in the catalogue as D-Ap5)
label: Full competitive NMDA-receptor block, the reference control
action: Competitive block of the glutamate site: the control against which any negative modulator is read.
rationale: It abolishes the spontaneous bursts, so it bounds how much NMDA-receptor current must go before the burst stops.
open_premise: That the burst needs NMDA-receptor activity does not show a gain of receptor function.
counter: Against the wild-type floor about 20 percent of the delayed evoked response remains under it (figure-read, inference), which is not evidence of incomplete block.
next_test: Measure the abolition threshold (percent of isolated NMDA-receptor current removed) with measured bath magnesium; this is the first number every NAM comparison needs.
moves: A clean abolition threshold, measured on the isolated NMDA-receptor current, fixes the reference; nothing lowers it, it is the control.

label: Ifenprodil-site GluN2B negative modulator, used as a tool
action: Negative allosteric modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors at the ifenprodil site.
rationale: A burst effect at a smaller removed fraction than the control needs would make a GluN2B-directed comparison the better question.
open_premise: The removable share of such a modulator is bounded by receptor composition and zinc, so a plateau below the control is unresolved, not support for total gain.
counter: The compound's GluN2B rows are measured activities, not a curated mechanism, and other targets are also measured; selectivity is not assessed.
next_test: Measure its removable fraction in the isolated NMDA-receptor current first; compare with the control only up to that fraction. A second modulator of the same site controls chemotype only.
moves: Up: a removable fraction at the burst clearly below the abolition threshold. Down: a plateau below the threshold, which stays unresolved rather than refuting the mechanism.

name_full: GYKI 53655; GYKI 52466 (a different structure, not the same compound); NBQX; perampanel
label: AMPA/kainate block arm: a pair of two mechanisms
action: Block of AMPA and kainate receptors with a noncompetitive 2,3-benzodiazepine and, as the independent partner, the competitive NBQX; perampanel shares the benzodiazepine's pocket and serves as a same-site cross-check.
rationale: Survival of the burst under a verified block would remove an AMPA contribution; abolition alone cannot separate AMPA drive from loss of magnesium relief.
open_premise: Whether an AMPA-dependent component exists at all; the 90 percent design value of the block is at the edge of what the tool gives in tissue (80-89 percent at 10 uM).
counter: The nearest tissue precedent, evoked Up states of barrel cortex, persisted under the benzodiazepine (transfer, with limits); two compounds are registered under one GYKI label; kainate is not separated.
next_test: Measure the achieved block and the NMDA-receptor current at the working concentration; test survival of the bursts under a verified block; d-APV only if bursts persist.
moves: Up for the survival question: bursts persisting under a verified block. Down: abolition, which does not separate the explanations.

label: Ih (HCN) blocker as a tool arm, after matched-condition recordings
action: Block of the hyperpolarisation-activated current, two chemotypes, engagement shown first.
rationale: Only worth running if sag and rebound stay larger at matched potential and deflection.
open_premise: Whether any HCN contribution remains after matching; no benefit is claimed.
counter: A blocker response shows contribution as in normal cortex, not a defect; the passive-size reading is the rival; a sodium-current block is reported for one tool in thalamic neurons (abstract level).
next_test: Run the matched-condition recording with capacitance and access resistance first; no HCN compound is nominated before it.
moves: Up: the excess sag persisting at matched potential and deflection. Down: it vanishing, or the blocker-sensitive current per capacitance being the same.

label: Clinical-stage GluN2B negative modulator with an assembly-dependent maximum
action: Negative modulation of GluN2B-containing receptors; maximum inhibition 82 percent on rat GluN1/GluN2B against 45 percent on rat triheteromers (human GluN1/GluN2B 91 percent).
rationale: A clinical-stage compound (catalogue maximum phase 2) that could serve as the in-slice modulator once the tool result is in.
open_premise: That the ceiling seen in oocytes holds in the slice; its washout is very slow in oocytes.
counter: The selectivity statement rests on a supplementary figure that was not read; slice precedent is a different region and age.
next_test: Use only after V02 shows a removable fraction; read the fraction at the burst, not in oocytes.
moves: Up: a removable fraction already shown by the tool. Down: a ceiling like the tool's, which adds a chemotype and nothing else.

label: Human-exposure GluN2B negative modulator found by the search, site not recorded
action: Negative modulation of the GluN2B subunit; the receptor site is not recorded.
rationale: A second modulator with human exposure could extend the comparison, if it acts at the ifenprodil site.
open_premise: Whether it shares the ifenprodil site and the triheteromer ceiling; the registry gives no receptor site.
counter: Abstract-level source only: a phase 2 study in adults with depression.
next_test: Find a primary source stating its site and maximum effect on triheteromers (public, in silico); until then it is not a same-site control.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) row: human GluN2B, negative allosteric modulator, pIC50 8.08 (the 8.3 in the original-affinity field is the same datum as an IC50 in nM), sourced to a patent, selectivity not determined, no assay text and no receptor site.
moves: Up: a primary source placing it at the ifenprodil site with a clearly different triheteromer maximum, or at a different documented site that gives a different comparison. Down: the same site and a similar ceiling. Otherwise unresolved.

label: pH-dependent GluN2B modulator: a condition to state, not a candidate
action: Inhibition of GluN2B-containing receptors, stronger at acidic pH.
rationale: It shows that GluN2B-directed potency can depend on the bath pH.
open_premise: Whether ifenprodil-site modulators in general depend on pH enough to matter in the slice.
next_test: State and match the bath pH in every arm; check the literature on pH dependence of the tool actually used.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) row: inhibition of human GluN2B in oocytes at pH 6.9, pIC50 7.64, selectivity not determined; the registry flags the compound as approved while ChEMBL gives maximum phase 1 (the flag is not carried).
moves: Up: evidence that ifenprodil-site modulators in general depend on pH enough to matter in the slice. Down: a dependence specific to this molecule or irrelevant at the slice pH.

label: Class recorded on a GluN1/GluN2B assembly record, no maximum effect
action: Antagonism recorded on the two-gene GRIN1/GRIN2B record of a curated mechanism table.
rationale: Possible chemotype controls if V02 and V05 do not give one.
open_premise: That an assembly record means subunit selectivity: it names where the mechanism was attached, not how selective the molecule is.
counter: No maximum effect, species or assay context in the catalogue; no approval statement in the catalogue.
next_test: Read primary sources for maximum effect and site only if a further chemotype is needed.
registry_note: Registry (ChEMBL 37) curated mechanism rows: antagonist on the record GRIN1/GRIN2B (two genes), maximum phase 2 or lower.
moves: Up: a primary source giving site and maximum effect. Down: nothing needed unless the tool and the clinical-stage compound do not give a chemotype control.

label: Registry row under GluN2B whose assay text names GluN2C
action: Recorded as a negative modulator under a GluN2B entry.
open_premise: The registry row's assay text names another subunit; to which subunit the value belongs is unresolved, so no GluN2B statement is drawn.
counter: Filing under a target does not make the measurement the target's; the same ligand has its own rows for other subunits, and no transfer is made.
next_test: None; kept so the filing is not mistaken for evidence.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) row filed under rat Grin2b: negative modulator, pIC50 6.95; its assay text says GluN1-1a co-expressed with GluN2C; the same ligand has its own GluN2C row (pIC50 8.15) and a GluN2D row, and the 6.95 differs from both.
moves: Nothing moves it: kept so the filing is not mistaken for evidence. Reopen if the primary paper assigns the value to GluN2B.

label: Kv7 opening and gap-junction block: abstain
action: Opening of Kv7 channels, or block of connexin and pannexin channels, proposed in earlier readings.
rationale: A response would not show a defect of the target in these cells.
open_premise: That a leak deficit or coupling drives the burst: neither is shown; the burst fall under the gap-junction tool has no supporting datum for coupling.
counter: Smaller cells with a seal leak, and effects on synaptic currents seen in culture, would give the same observations.
next_test: Nominate nothing before a difference current reversing near the potassium equilibrium potential and a matched-effect control that fails to reproduce the fall.
moves: Up: a difference current reversing near the potassium equilibrium potential in Wwox neurons, and a matched-effect control that fails to reproduce the fall. Down: passive size with a seal leak explaining the observations.

name_full: tiagabine; NNC-711; other selective GAT-1 inhibitors as tools
label: Supply-side GABA lever: block of GABA reuptake, a different question from receptor potentiation
action: Block of the GABA transporter GAT-1 raises GABA availability without touching glutamate-receptor currents; the catalogue records maximum phase 4 for one reference compound and lists several selective tools.
rationale: It separates a deficit of GABA supply from a postsynaptic or chloride-gradient deficit: only the first is helped by more GABA.
open_premise: Whether the halved inhibitory current is a supply deficit; the direction depends on the chloride gradient of the preparation, which is unmeasured.
counter: In the repository's own records raising GABAergic tone is unresolved (an irreversible inactivator of GABA transaminase resolved spasms in one of two children, partly in the other, with null reports elsewhere, and carries a brain-imaging signal); a compensatory change in tonic inhibition or transporter expression could mask the effect.
next_test: Evoked IPSC amplitude, E/I ratio and the chloride reversal potential first; then the lever against a GABA-A potentiator and a non-GABAergic suppression, each matched to the same measured effect.
moves: Up: a low evoked IPSC with a hyperpolarising chloride gradient and a lever effect above the matched non-GABAergic control. Down: a response-side deficit, or depolarising GABA.

label: GABA-transaminase block: affinities of irreversible inhibitors are not a potency ranking
action: Inactivation of GABA transaminase raises GABA; the registry rows are affinity values for compounds that act irreversibly.
rationale: It is the other way to raise GABA availability, kept so that the two ways are not mixed.
open_premise: That a lower affinity number means a weaker compound: for irreversible inactivators the number does not measure it.
counter: The repository already records that the older drug resolved spasms in one child and carries a brain-imaging safety signal; the newer one is clinical-stage only (catalogue maximum phase 1).
next_test: No comparison before an inactivation parameter is available; start from the supply-side question of V11.
registry_note: Registry (GtoPdb 2026.3.1) rows on human ABAT: pKi 3.07 for the older drug (labelled irreversible inhibition) and pKi 5.01 for the newer one (labelled inhibition); 4-acryloylphenol has a pIC50 and its primary target in the registry is another enzyme (ABAT is non-primary). The values are not a potency ranking of irreversible inactivators.
moves: Nothing moves it until an inactivation measure exists; then up if the newer compound shows a clearly larger inactivation rate under the same assay.
